newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton futures called to open 0.10 higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton futures called to open 0.10 higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent per lb firmer based on market orders at 1017 EDT and following a mostly neutral monthly supply and demand report, traders said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture pegged output at 17.8 million (480-lb) bales in 1997/98 compared with the July estimate of 18.0 million bales.
Industry analysts had pegged the USDA estimate between 17.47 million and 18.15 million bales.
The USDA left exports unchanged at 7.10 million bales and lowered ending stocks to 3.80 million bales versus last month's estimate of 3.95 million bales.
World production fell to 86.91 million bales from 87.50 million bales in July, and ending stocks to 35.24 million bales from 35.31 million bales.
Also, NYCE reported that the speculators held a net short position of 13.2 percent as of August 8.
Monday, most active December cotton closed 0.55 cent lower at 73.76 cents a lb, while the rest of the board settled 0.08 to 0.58 cent weaker.
An estimated 15,000 lots changed hands on the day.
Nearby resistance was pegged at 74.00 cents followed by 75.20 cents basis December.
